entryPointCandidates.name: 01_multi_threaded.py
entryPointCandidates.summary: Demonstrates basic Python multithreading by splitting the same summation workload across two Thread instances running the shared my_sum function concurrently, with start/join semantics explained in comments.

entryPointCandidates.name: 02_multi_threaded_local_data.py
entryPointCandidates.summary: Variant of the multithreaded summation example that introduces threading.local() to illustrate (and contrast against) explicit thread-local storage, though the accumulator is still a plain local variable in practice.

entryPointCandidates.name: 03extra_minimal_race_condition.py
entryPointCandidates.summary: Minimal reproducible race condition example spawning 10 threads that all increment a shared global counter without locking, typically producing a final value less than the expected 10,000,000 due to lost updates.

entryPointCandidates.name: 04_multi_threaded_lock.py
entryPointCandidates.summary: Fixes the race condition from the nolock example by wrapping the shared-state mutation of COMMON_COUNTER and COMMON_LIST in a threading.Lock acquire/release pair, guaranteeing consistent results across concurrent threads.

file:parallel/00_single_threaded.py.name: 00_single_threaded.py
file:parallel/00_single_threaded.py.summary: Baseline script that sums a large range of integers single-threaded and times the execution, used as a performance reference point before introducing threading.

function:parallel/00_single_threaded.py:.name: my_sum
function:parallel/00_single_threaded.py:.summary: Sums integers in the range [a, b) in a simple loop and prints the result.

file:parallel/01_multi_threaded.py.name: 01_multi_threaded.py
file:parallel/01_multi_threaded.py.summary: Demonstrates basic Python multithreading by splitting the same summation workload across two Thread instances running the shared my_sum function concurrently, with start/join semantics explained in comments.

function:parallel/01_multi_threaded.py:m.name: my_sum
function:parallel/01_multi_threaded.py:m.summary: Sums integers in the range [a, b) and prints the result; invoked concurrently by two threads splitting the workload in half.

file:parallel/02_multi_threaded_local_da.name: 02_multi_threaded_local_data.py
file:parallel/02_multi_threaded_local_da.summary: Variant of the multithreaded summation example that introduces threading.local() to illustrate (and contrast against) explicit thread-local storage, though the accumulator is still a plain local variable in practice.

function:parallel/02_multi_threaded_loca.name: my_sum
function:parallel/02_multi_threaded_loca.summary: Sums integers in the range [a, b), initializing a threading.local() instance to demonstrate thread-local memory before falling back to a plain per-call accumulator.

file:parallel/03_multi_threaded_nolock.p.name: 03_multi_threaded_nolock.py
file:parallel/03_multi_threaded_nolock.p.summary: Demonstrates a race condition by having two threads concurrently mutate shared global state (COMMON_COUNTER and COMMON_LIST) without synchronization, then cross-checks and highlights the resulting inconsistency in red using colorama.

function:parallel/03_multi_threaded_nolo.name: my_sum_mod
function:parallel/03_multi_threaded_nolo.summary: Sums integers in [a, b) while unsynchronized-mutating shared globals COMMON_COUNTER and COMMON_LIST whenever a value is a multiple of m, exposing a race condition across concurrent threads.

file:parallel/03extra_minimal_race_condi.name: 03extra_minimal_race_condition.py
file:parallel/03extra_minimal_race_condi.summary: Minimal reproducible race condition example spawning 10 threads that all increment a shared global counter without locking, typically producing a final value less than the expected 10,000,000 due to lost updates.

function:parallel/03extra_minimal_race_c.name: increment
function:parallel/03extra_minimal_race_c.summary: Increments a shared global counter max_val times without synchronization, used as the target function for 10 concurrent threads to expose a race condition.

file:parallel/04_multi_threaded_lock.py.name: 04_multi_threaded_lock.py
file:parallel/04_multi_threaded_lock.py.summary: Fixes the race condition from the nolock example by wrapping the shared-state mutation of COMMON_COUNTER and COMMON_LIST in a threading.Lock acquire/release pair, guaranteeing consistent results across concurrent threads.

function:parallel/04_multi_threaded_lock.name: my_sum_mod
function:parallel/04_multi_threaded_lock.summary: Sums integers in [a, b) while safely mutating shared globals COMMON_COUNTER and COMMON_LIST inside a lock-protected critical section whenever a value is a multiple of m.

file:parallel/04extra_minimal_race_condi.name: 04extra_minimal_race_condition_with_lock.py
file:parallel/04extra_minimal_race_condi.summary: Minimal demonstration of a race condition fix using threading.Lock, where 10 threads increment a shared global counter safely inside a critical section.

function:parallel/04extra_minimal_race_c.name: increment
function:parallel/04extra_minimal_race_c.summary: Increments a shared global counter max_val times, guarding each increment with a lock acquire/release to avoid a race condition.

file:parallel/05_multi_threaded_pool_loc.name: 05_multi_threaded_pool_lock.py
file:parallel/05_multi_threaded_pool_loc.summary: Demonstrates ThreadPoolExecutor with a shared Lock to safely aggregate a common counter and list while four threads each sum a partition of a large range.

function:parallel/05_multi_threaded_pool.name: my_sum_mod
function:parallel/05_multi_threaded_pool.summary: Sums integers in [a, b) and, for multiples of m, safely updates a shared counter and list under a lock; returns the partial sum.

file:parallel/06_multi_threaded_pool_que.name: 06_multi_threaded_pool_queue.py
file:parallel/06_multi_threaded_pool_que.summary: Demonstrates ThreadPoolExecutor combined with a thread-safe queue.Queue as an alternative to explicit locking for collecting values found by concurrent worker threads.

function:parallel/06_multi_threaded_pool.name: my_sum_mod
function:parallel/06_multi_threaded_pool.summary: Sums integers in [a, b) and pushes multiples of m onto a shared thread-safe queue instead of using a lock; returns the partial sum.

file:parallel/07_multi_processing.py.name: 07_multi_processing.py
file:parallel/07_multi_processing.py.summary: Basic example of true parallelism using multiprocessing.Process, spawning two separate OS processes that each sum half of a large integer range concurrently.

function:parallel/07_multi_processing.py.name: my_sum
function:parallel/07_multi_processing.py.summary: Sums integers in the range [a, b) and prints the result; used as the target function for each spawned process.

file:parallel/08_multi_processing_pool_s.name: 08_multi_processing_pool_starmap.py
file:parallel/08_multi_processing_pool_s.summary: Demonstrates multiprocessing.Pool.starmap to distribute a range-sum computation across 4 worker processes with a blocking call that returns all results at once.

function:parallel/08_multi_processing_po.name: my_sum
function:parallel/08_multi_processing_po.summary: Sums integers in the range [a, b), prints, and returns the result; distributed across a process pool via starmap.

file:parallel/09_multi_processing_pool_s.name: 09_multi_processing_pool_starmapasync.py
file:parallel/09_multi_processing_pool_s.summary: Demonstrates the non-blocking multiprocessing.Pool.starmap_async API, polling readiness in a loop while sub-processes compute partial sums in the background.

function:parallel/09_multi_processing_po.name: my_sum
function:parallel/09_multi_processing_po.summary: Sums integers in the range [a, b), prints, and returns the result; distributed asynchronously across a process pool via starmap_async.

file:parallel/cpu_intensive.py.name: cpu_intensive.py
file:parallel/cpu_intensive.py.summary: Sequential baseline for a CPU-bound Monte Carlo integration benchmark, running 10 chunks of a numerical integration one after another without any concurrency.

function:parallel/cpu_intensive.py:f.name: f
function:parallel/cpu_intensive.py:f.summary: Arbitrary mathematical function sin(1/(x*(2-x)))^2 used as the integrand for the Monte Carlo integration.

function:parallel/cpu_intensive.py:cpu_f.name: cpu_function
function:parallel/cpu_intensive.py:cpu_f.summary: Performs a seeded Monte Carlo integration of f(x) over 2 million random samples and returns the hit count and sample size.

file:parallel/cpu_intensive_threading.py.name: cpu_intensive_threading.py
file:parallel/cpu_intensive_threading.py.summary: Runs the same CPU-bound Monte Carlo integration as cpu_intensive.py but distributes the 10 chunks across a ThreadPoolExecutor, illustrating that threading provides no speedup for CPU-bound work due to the GIL.

function:parallel/cpu_intensive_threadin.name: f
function:parallel/cpu_intensive_threadin.summary: Arbitrary mathematical function sin(1/(x*(2-x)))^2 used as the integrand for the Monte Carlo integration.

function:parallel/cpu_intensive_threadin.name: cpu_function
function:parallel/cpu_intensive_threadin.summary: Performs a seeded Monte Carlo integration of f(x) over 2 million random samples and returns the hit count and sample size; submitted as a task to a ThreadPoolExecutor.

file:parallel/cpu_intensive_multiprocess.name: cpu_intensive_multiprocessing.py
file:parallel/cpu_intensive_multiprocess.summary: Runs the same CPU-bound Monte Carlo integration as cpu_intensive.py but distributes the 10 chunks across separate processes, demonstrating real parallel speedup for CPU-bound work by bypassing the GIL.

function:parallel/cpu_intensive_multipro.name: f
function:parallel/cpu_intensive_multipro.summary: Arbitrary mathematical function sin(1/(x*(2-x)))^2 used as the integrand for the Monte Carlo integration.

function:parallel/cpu_intensive_multipro.name: cpu_function
function:parallel/cpu_intensive_multipro.summary: Performs a seeded Monte Carlo integration of f(x) over 2 million random samples and returns the hit count and sample size; distributed across worker processes.

file:parallel/io_intensive.py.name: io_intensive.py
file:parallel/io_intensive.py.summary: Sequential baseline for an I/O-bound benchmark that downloads a list of remote image URLs one at a time and saves each to disk under a content-hashed filename.

function:parallel/io_intensive.py:io_fun.name: io_function
function:parallel/io_intensive.py:io_fun.summary: Fetches a remote file over HTTP, computes an MD5 hash of its content for the filename, and writes the file to the local pics directory.

file:parallel/io_intensive_threading.py.name: io_intensive_threading.py
file:parallel/io_intensive_threading.py.summary: Runs the same I/O-bound URL-fetching benchmark as io_intensive.py but distributes the downloads across a ThreadPoolExecutor, showing that threading speeds up I/O-bound work because the GIL is released during blocking network calls.

function:parallel/io_intensive_threading.name: io_function
function:parallel/io_intensive_threading.summary: Fetches a remote file over HTTP, computes an MD5 hash of its content for the filename, and writes the file to the local pics directory; submitted as a task to a ThreadPoolExecutor.

file:parallel/io_intensive_multiprocessi.name: io_intensive_multiprocessing.py
file:parallel/io_intensive_multiprocessi.summary: Runs the same I/O-bound URL-fetching benchmark as io_intensive.py but distributes the downloads across separate processes, used to compare process-based vs thread-based vs sequential I/O concurrency.

function:parallel/io_intensive_multiproc.name: io_function
function:parallel/io_intensive_multiproc.summary: Fetches a remote file over HTTP, computes an MD5 hash of its content for the filename, and writes the file to the local pics directory; distributed across worker processes.

file:spark/notebooks/utils/producer.py.name: producer.py
file:spark/notebooks/utils/producer.py.summary: Standalone TCP socket server that generates randomized fake transaction records (name, surname, amount, delta_t, flag) as JSON lines and streams them to a connected client, used as the data source for the Lecture 3 Structured Streaming exercises.

function:spark/notebooks/utils/producer..name: send_messages
function:spark/notebooks/utils/producer..summary: Continuously generates a random transaction-like JSON message and sends it, newline-terminated, over the given client socket every 0.2 seconds until interrupted or the socket errors out.
